title: Console: Triage and Reduce Scope for Core Metrics & Tracing MVP
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures a focused scope reduction for the Redwood Console observability workstream. The goal is to ship a small, high-value MVP of Metrics, Cost Breakdown, and Tracing that provides immediate product-level insights while deferring higher-effort features that threaten schedule. This document records the reduced scope, acceptance criteria for the cut MVP, rationale for each cut, and rollout plan.
scope_included: Dashboard landing with three core panels: Request rate & error rate, 95th/99th latency by model, and token cost per-route (24h/7d)
Per-model time series (per-hour) for throughput and median latency (last 7 days)
Basic cost breakdown: per-route and per-model totals with CSV export for last 24h and 7d
Lightweight request tracing: sampled traces at 1% of requests with direct link to request record and basic timeline view
Alerting stub: threshold-based alerts configurable per-route (UI to set threshold, backend hook to create alert rule)
RBAC: console view restricted by existing role (viewer/editor) — no new permission model in MVP
Telemetry retention: 30 days for aggregated metrics and sampled traces
scope_removed: Per-token heatmap / token-level cost drilldown (deferred to Phase 2)
Full-fidelity per-request trace capture at 100% sampling (deferred)
Longer retention tiers (90/365 days) and tiered storage management
Per-customer cost allocation UI for multi-tenant orgs (post-MVP analytics add-on)
Automatic anomaly detection and ML-driven regressions
Deep trace -> logs correlation UI (link only in MVP)
Per-token cost attribution in real-time during streaming responses
acceptance_criteria: Landing dashboard reachable from Console nav and rendering within 1.5s under normal load
Three core panels show accurate aggregated numbers with correct units (requests, errors, ms, tokens, USD) and match backend metrics for sample queries
CSV export returns correct aggregated rows for requested window (24h / 7d) and downloadable within 20s for a 7d query
Tracing pipeline stores sampled trace events and UI can render a trace timeline for sampled requests; trace link opens to raw trace JSON via existing logs URL
Cost breakdown view shows per-route and per-model totals and toggles between 24h and 7d, numbers reconcile with billing exports within 5% margin
RBAC enforcement prevents users without viewer role from accessing the dashboard pages
Smoke tests added to CI that verify dashboard endpoint responds and key panels contain non-empty data using test fixtures
rationale: Shipping a minimal set of dashboards gives product teams immediate visibility into production regressions without delaying delivery for advanced analytics features
Per-token and 100% trace capture are high engineering costs and large storage expenses; deferring reduces unknown infra risk for the release window
Sampling traces at 1% provides a signal for performance investigations while keeping storage and indexing costs bounded
CSV export provides a pragmatic way for customers to perform deeper ad-hoc analyses while we iterate on richer UIs
tradeoffs: Lower trace sampling increases time-to-detect rare, high-latency outliers — mitigated by retaining 30-day aggregates and alerting
Deferred multi-tenant cost allocation reduces immediate value for internal platforms teams but preserves delivery velocity
Simpler RBAC keeps scope small but may require quick follow-up if customers need finer-grained controls
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internals): wireframe sign-off by PM + Design, finalize API contracts with ENG (2 days)
Phase 1 (backend): enable aggregated metric ingest endpoints and CSV export API (ENG-6124) (2 sprints)
Phase 2 (frontend): implement dashboard pages, panels, traces UI and basic RBAC checks (1 sprint)
Phase 3 (QA & Beta): internal beta with 3 pilot customers, run reconciliation tests against billing exports, collect feedback (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (GA): enable feature flag rollout to all orgs, monitor cost & SLOs, prepare backlog for Phase 2 features
dependencies_notes: ENG-6124: metrics ingestion schema must be finalized and backwards compatible with existing telemetry pipeline
ENG-6340: CSV export relies on background query worker and S3 temporary storage — needs capacity reservation
ENG-7012: tracing storage TTL change and sampling config endpoints must be available before UI toggles sampling rates
Design: mockups for the three panels and export modal (see attachments)
open_questions: Should sample rate be configurable per-org in MVP or remain a global flag? (current lean decision: global)
Do we need cost conversions for multiple billing currencies in MVP? (lean decision: show USD only for GA customers with billing data)
What threshold defaults should we ship for alerting? (suggest 95th latency breach: 2x baseline, and error rate >= 1%)
post_acceptance_followups: Create Phase 2 ticket for per-token heatmap and trace->log correlation (PM-7602)
Define retention tiering and pricing implications with Finance
Schedule security review for trace storage and PII redaction prior to retention >30 days
notes: This ticket is intentionally prescriptive about cuts to avoid scope creep in the next planning horizon. Engineering and Design asked for a firm cut list to avoid feature-by-feature debates during sprint execution. We'll convert remaining deferred items into tracked follow-ups with prioritization criteria tied to customer requests and cost/infra feasibility.
